process_area.title: Grievance Handling, Labor Dispute & DOLE Conciliation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logs in grievance case system" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documents Step-1 decision" (replaces manual Step 3).
Pain Points / Risks: - **Process risk**: Missed CBA timeline forfeits management defense; mitigated by SLA-bounded case system
System Touchpoints: - Grievance case system; CBA-prescribed timelines; documentation repository

steps.activity: HR receives grievance (written/verbal via union or individual); logs in grievance case system; classifies (wage, discipline, working condition, interpretation)
HR convenes Step-1 conference with employee, union steward, and immediate supervisor within CBA-prescribed timeline (often 5–7 days)
HR documents Step-1 decision; communicates to employee/union; escalates to Step-2 if unresolved

fields.Participants: LR Director, HR, Union, Senior Management

workflows.name: Grievance Escalation, Step-2/3 Review & CBA Dispute Resolution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review with higher management and union officers" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documents final position" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-482 (ensure controlled execution — Grievance Handling, Labor Dispute & DOLE Conciliation (PA-84.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Escalation risk**: Repeated unresolved grievances signal systemic issues; mitigated by root-cause analysis
System Touchpoints: - Grievance case escalation workflow; documentation repository

steps.activity: LR Director convenes Step-2 review with higher management and union officers; reviews evidence and prior decision
LR Director facilitates Step-3 (grievance committee or top management) per CBA; seeks resolution before arbitration
LR Director documents final position; if unresolved, advises on DOLE SENA/NLRC arbitration pathway

workflows.name: Preventive Suspension, Due Process & Notice Workflow (2-Notice Rule)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-issue of "issues Notice of Preventive Suspension" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documents employee response" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-482 (ensure controlled execution — Grievance Handling, Labor Dispute & DOLE Conciliation (PA-84.2).)
- operational: standardized workflow and legal review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Legal risk**: Procedural defect (no 2-notice) makes dismissal illegal; mitigated by standardized workflow and legal review
System Touchpoints: - Disciplinary case system; notice templates; timeline tracker

steps.activity: HR issues Notice of Preventive Suspension (not exceeding 30 days per Labor Code) with written grounds; ensures pay rules per law
HR serves First Notice (Notice to Explain) specifying charges and giving employee opportunity to respond within reasonable period (typically 5 days)
HR documents employee response; prepares for hearing and decision; safeguards against procedural defects

fields.Participants: LR Director, HR, Legal, Employee, Union, Witnesses

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "LR Director/Legal evaluates evidence against just causes" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-file of "HR issues Second Notice" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-482 (ensure controlled execution — Grievance Handling, Labor Dispute & DOLE Conciliation (PA-84.2).)
- operational: hearing rigor and proportionality assessment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Legal risk**: Insufficient evidence or disproportionate penalty; mitigated by hearing rigor and proportionality assessment
System Touchpoints: - Disciplinary case file; hearing record; decision repository

steps.activity: LR Director conducts administrative hearing; presents evidence; allows employee (with counsel/union rep) to cross-examine and present defense
LR Director/Legal evaluates evidence against just causes (serious misconduct, willful disobedience, fraud, etc.); documents findings
HR issues Second Notice (Decision) with penalty and rationale; communicates appeal rights; archives complete case file

fields.Participants: LR Director, Legal, DOLE Conciliator-Mediator, Employee/Union
fields.Trigger: Unresolved grievance or labor standards complaint

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "LR Director negotiates settlement where commercially and legally sound" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "prepares referral and representation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-482 (ensure controlled execution — Grievance Handling, Labor Dispute & DOLE Conciliation (PA-84.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Settlement risk**: Premature/unfavorable settlement; mitigated by costing and legal review
System Touchpoints: - SENA case file; settlement documentation; DOLE portal

steps.activity: LR Director participates in DOLE Single-Entry Approach (SENA) within 30-day conciliation-mediation; presents position and seeks settlement
LR Director negotiates settlement where commercially and legally sound; documents agreement; ensures compliance execution
If unresolved, case proceeds to Labor Arbitration; LR Director prepares referral and representation

fields.Participants: LR Director, External Labor Counsel, Legal, NLRC
fields.Trigger: SENA referral or direct filing at NLRC

steps.activity: External Labor Counsel files position paper and represents company at Labor Arbitration; presents evidence and witnesses
LR Director coordinates evidence and witnesses; reviews strategy; manages settlement discussions during arbitration
Legal files appeal to NLRC Commission or Court of Appeals where warranted; executes final decision; tracks compliance

workflows.name: Illegal Dismissal, Reinstatement & Backpay Compliance Execution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-update of "updates policy/training to prevent recurrence" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-482 (ensure controlled execution — Grievance Handling, Labor Dispute & DOLE Conciliation (PA-84.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost/reputational risk**: Non-execution invites contempt; mitigated by prompt compliance
System Touchpoints: - Backpay computation; payroll restoration; case closure

steps.activity: HR/Legal computes backwages (from dismissal to finality) and separation pay (if reinstatement infeasible) per decision
HR executes reinstatement or separation per decision and employee election; restores benefits/seniority if reinstated
Finance processes payment; LR Director closes case and archives; updates policy/training to prevent recurrence

fields.Frequency: Continuous intake; annual committee constitution and code re-publication; case-driven investigations. Formal cases: ~10–30/year chain-wide (benchmark range for a 6,762-employee multi-site retailer, understated by underreporting without a trusted channel)
fields.Participants: CODI Chair & Members (HR, supervisory, rank-and-file, union representative where a CBA unit exists), HR Manager, CHRO, Legal Counsel (VS-100), EAP Manager/OH Nurse (VS-83), IT Security (online-conduct evidence, VS-27), DOLE (reporting/jurisdictional interfaces)
fields.Trigger: (a) Report/complaint of sexual harassment or gender-based sexual harassment (GBSH) — work-related superior/subordinate, peer-to-peer, client/customer-to-employee, or online conduct against an employee; (b) annual CODI constitution/reconstitution cycle; (c) policy or regulatory change
fields.Volume: All 6,762 employees across 205 sites + ~10–20% contingent workers (VS-98) are in scope; both laws apply to every BuildRight entity with 10+ employees (all 205 sites qualify). One CODI per legal entity (5), each supported by trained case handlers; awareness training reaches 100% of employees annually (~6,762 completions)

workflows.name: POSH / Safe Spaces Compliance Program — CODI Committee, Statutory Investigation & Reporting (RA 7877 / RA 11313)

Automation Opportunity: - Case-intake form auto-creates the confidential case record with the statutory clock started and restricted-access flag applied (replaces manual Step 3 registration).
- SLA timer escalates to the CODI chair and CHRO when an investigation approaches the statutory deadline (supports Step 5).
- Anonymized case-statistics dashboard auto-assembles the quarterly board-committee extract (replaces manual Step 9 compilation).
Background: RA 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act, 1995) obliges employers to promulgate rules and constitute a **Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CODI)** for sexual-harassment cases involving authority/influence relationships. RA 11313 (Safe Spaces Act, 2019) expanded coverage to **peer, client/customer-to-employee, and online gender-based sexual harassment** and requires employers with 10+ employees to adopt a code of conduct and investigation machinery — retail is acutely exposed because ~5,800 frontline staff serve 2.8M monthly customer interactions. Prior coverage was step-level only: the annual anti-harassment refresher inside W719 (VS-19.1 DEI) and generic grievance intake in W2881 — no workflow owned the statutory CODI machinery. Distinct from: W2881/W2882 (CBA grievance steps), W2884 (general disciplinary investigation — this workflow's statutory sibling with its own committee and confidentiality regime), W2943/VS-119 (ethics/ABC speak-up), W1733 (channel administration), VS-159.3 (security/workplace-violence investigations), VS-100 (litigation once cases escalate).
Controls: - CTL-482 (ensure controlled execution — Grievance Handling, Labor Dispute & DOLE Conciliation (PA-84.2).)
Cross-references: - W2881/W2882 (general grievance machinery), W2883/W2884 (due process & disciplinary investigation), W2885 (SENA), W2888 (strike contingency — harassment-case mishandling is a known labor-relations flashpoint)
- W719 (VS-19.1 annual anti-harassment refresher — training slice), W51 (training records), W2865 (EAP counseling), W2866 (RA 11036 program)

- W1721 (Audit Committee reporting), W1733/W356 (speak-up channels & non-retaliation audit), VS-100 (litigation), VS-119 (ethics), VS-159.3 (workplace-violence investigations), VS-91 (RA 10173 case data), VS-98 (contingent workers), VS-103.2 (ESS/intranet publication)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Retaliation risk**: complainants transferred, downgraded, or frozen out after filing — defeats the statute's purpose and creates NLRC exposure; mitigated by 6–12-month retaliation watch tied to the non-retaliation audit (W356) and manager accountability

- **Confidentiality/gag-order breach**: identities leaked through case files or gossip — re-traumatizes complainants and deters reporting; mitigated by restricted-access case class, masked case lists, and sanctioned breach handling

- **Misclassification risk**: treating an RA 11313 customer-to-employee GBSH complaint as an ordinary customer-complaint (VS-13) or a W2881 grievance forfeits statutory protection; mitigated by the step-4 jurisdiction gate and CODI training

- **Underreporting**: benchmark incidence suggests retail harassment reports understate reality; mitigated by trusted multi-channel intake, visible CODI membership at store level, and annual awareness campaigns
- **Evidence spoliation**: online-conduct evidence (deleted chats/posts) lost before preservation; mitigated by immediate IT Security preservation request with chain-of-custody logging
- **CODI capacity/conflict**: committee members investigating their own chain of command; mitigated by cross-entity member pools and external counsel support for senior-respondent cases
System Touchpoints: - HR case management: confidential POSH/GBSH case type with restricted-access role (complainant/respondent identities masked in general case lists), statutory-clock SLA timer, and evidence attachments with chain-of-custody metadata
- ESS confidential reporting form (anonymous option for initial intake) routed only to CODI chair + Labor Relations Director
- Policy-acknowledgment tracking object for the annual code re-publication (W51-pattern completion records)
- Disciplinary-action object for sanction posting (integration with W2884 due-process notices)
- Anonymized case-statistics extract to the board-committee reporting pack (W1721)
Time Estimate: - Per formal case: ~30–60 hours end-to-end across CODI, HR, and Legal spread over 30–45 calendar days
- Program overhead: ~15–20 days/year (constitution, code, training liaison, analytics) — absorbed by Labor Relations Director + CODI members; no incremental headcount

steps.activity: Annual CODI constitution per entity: chair + members representing management, supervisory, and rank-and-file levels (plus the union representative where a bargaining unit exists — links to VS-84.1), with at least one member of each gender; publish committee membership, reporting channels, and the anti-harassment code on notice boards, ESS portal, and store huddle boards (links to VS-103.2 W3339)

Code of conduct maintenance: definitions under RA 7877 (authority/influence SH) and RA 11313 (peer, client-to-employee, online GBSH — including customer conduct toward cashiers, promodisers, and service-desk staff), examples, sanctions matrix, confidentiality/gag-order obligations, and whistleblower protection; annual employee acknowledgment captured in HR records (per W51 pattern)

Multi-channel intake: in-person (any manager, HR, or CODI member), ESS confidential form, hotline, or sealed written report; acknowledge within 24 hours; apply interim measures (schedule/location adjustment of the *respondent*, not the complainant; preventive suspension per W2883 where warranted); enforce gag order on disclosure of identities

Jurisdiction & classification: determine RA 7877 vs RA 11313 track; route adjacent matters — general grievances (W2881), ethics/corruption (VS-119), criminal conduct to Legal (VS-100) and PNP, customer-safety violence (VS-159.3); confirm CODI jurisdiction and statutory investigation clock

Investigation: documentary and interview evidence (complainant, respondent, witnesses) with RA 10173 safeguards (VS-91); written interview summaries; preservation of online-conduct evidence (messages, screenshots, posts) with IT Security chain-of-custody (VS-27); target completion within the statutory period (≤30 days from formal complaint)

Hearing & determination: both parties heard separately; CODI deliberates on preponderance of evidence; written report with findings, aggravating/mitigating factors, and recommended sanction aligned to the sanctions matrix; served with due-process notices (2-notice rule per W2883/W2884)

Decision implementation & appeal: management implements sanction (reprimand to dismissal), records in the disciplinary file; internal appeal per policy; Legal explains criminal/civil options to the complainant (VS-100); SENA referral if the matter ripens into a labor dispute (W2885)

Remediation & non-retaliation monitoring: workplace restoration (transfers, team reintegration), 6–12-month retaliation watch (assignments, ratings, schedules), EAP counseling for the complainant and affected witnesses (W2865), warning/supervision for substantiated-but-minor findings

Statutory reporting & records: DOLE reportorial/submission requirements as they apply to harassment cases and committee operations; anonymized quarterly case statistics to the Audit Committee (W1721); confidential case files retained per VS-88 retention schedule in a restricted-access class separate from ordinary personnel files

Annual program review: case analytics (types, locations, customer-vs-employee origin, cycle time), root-cause and hot-spot analysis with LP/VS-23 where patterns indicate risk, refresher-training refresh with W719, policy/code update, and awareness campaign reinforcement at town halls (W3340/W2890)
